day_shape: 64 items: IDF says it killed senior Hezbollah 'Badder Unit' commander Abu Hassan Alaa in Deir al-Zahrani plus two Gaza strikes, Iran army chief Hatami announces $30,000 bounty on US troops, Hamas delegation in Cairo with Kushner and Egyptian intel, nothing from UK Parliament or IAEA.

threads.label: Hezbollah commander killed in south Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF announced it killed Abu Hassan Alaa, a senior commander in Hezbollah's 'Badder Unit', in a weekend strike on Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon. The military said the strike responded to a Hezbollah explosive drone attack that seriously wounded three soldiers on Saturday.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and Cairo negotiations
threads.summary: The IDF said it carried out two strikes within an hour in Khan Younis and Nuseirat targeting a Palestinian Islamic Jihad and a Hamas operative, with Palestinian media reporting several injured. Defa Press and Jerusalem Post reported a Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya met Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad and Jared Kushner in Cairo to discuss the 15-point Board of Peace plan.

threads.label: Iran army chief announces US troop bounty
threads.summary: Defa Press and Jerusalem Post reported Iranian army commander-in-chief Amir Hatami announced a $30,000 reward for any Iranian serviceman who captures or kills an invading US serviceman. Hatami also said the Strait 'will never return to its former condition' and would be managed under Iranian arrangements.

threads.label: US weighs tougher Iran sanctions
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported the US is weighing tougher Iran sanctions, including measures targeting Chinese banks, oil buyers and entities helping fund Tehran's war effort. The IDF assessed that Hamas and Hezbollah have begun coordinating increased activity with Iranian assistance in recent weeks.

threads.label: Iran-Gulf disputes over captured personnel
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported an Iranian military official said Qatar should allow an Iranian team to investigate the fate of pilots Tehran says were captured by Qatari forces, and that Iran accused Kuwait of withholding information on four detained Iranians. A Gulf analyst told the Post that Iran struck Qatar and is now seeking to recast its strategy as victimhood.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure: fuel, media law, execution
threads.summary: Iran International reported the government is weighing three proposals to ration gasoline as war damage and import problems widen the fuel deficit, and named MP Jafar Pourkabgani as personally firing on January protesters per witnesses. Jerusalem Post reported parliament approved general principles of a bill criminalising interviews with media deemed hostile, and Iran executed a man convicted over the Karaj protest car-ramming.

threads.label: Regime war-victory messaging and Khamenei fortieth
threads.summary: Khamenei's office announced commemorations in Tehran, Qom and Mashhad marking the fortieth day of the funeral of 'Iran's martyr', while parliament speaker Qalibaf said on Defa Press that Iran had 'genuinely won' the war militarily and politically. IRIB and Defa Press amplified claims of indigenous air defence, a purported Pentagon report of 24 downed MQ-9 drones, and Yemeni warnings to Saudi Arabia.

events.summary_en: Hamas's negotiating delegation headed by Khalil al-Hayya, head of the movement's political office, met this afternoon in Cairo with Lieutenant General Hassan Rashad, Egypt's intelligence minister. The Hamas delegation presented the intelligence minister with a report on daily violations of the ceasefire agreement by the Zionist regime and stressed that the Zionists are shirking their responsibility to implement the Sharm El-Sheikh agreement and Donald Trump's alleged peace plan. Members of the delegation also provided comprehensive details about events in the West Bank, occupied Jerusalem and Zionist prisons, saying that Zionist actions constitute a destructive and dangerous policy.

events.title_en: Pope Leo calls for end to violence against Palestinians in West Bank
events.summary_en: Pope Leo, after a Christian religious ceremony at his residence in Castel Gandolfo near Rome, said: once again I call for an end to repeated violence against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank. He also urged the international community to advance a two-state solution, adding that this approach can pave the way for 'just and lasting peace'. These remarks come as Palestinian homes in the village of Qusra in the West Bank have been surrounded after water and electricity cuts. Human rights groups describe these actions as part of an organised effort to seize land.

events.title_en: Deployment of Rapid Support Forces reinforcements to the border with Ethiopia
events.summary_en: The Rapid Support Forces, by deploying equipment and reinforcements to the al-Fashaqah region, have strengthened their military presence near the Ethiopian border. The Rapid Support Forces, which support the government, have deployed new reinforcements near the disputed tri-border area of al-Fashaqah near Ethiopia. This region, which has previously been the scene of multiple clashes between Ethiopian forces and government-supporting forces, is again witnessing increased military activity. The deployment of these fresh forces follows escalating regional tensions between Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front and heightening differences between Sudan and Egypt over the al-Fashaqah triangle.
